items.title: Amos White Interview, 1958-08-23
items.q: this office had been the former office of one of the noted Negro writers, T. Thomas Fortune, whom the world recognizes as one of the greatest editorialists of his day and time.

ctx.x: After my marriage to the president's daughter, Roxabel, I took residence in Jacksonville. And my first job was as a printer with the Florida Union Printing Company. Mrs. Saunders owned it. She was a very wealthy Negro woman down there. And this office had been the former office of one of the noted Negro writers, T. Thomas Fortune, whom the world recognizes as one of the greatest editorialists of his day and time. So I worked there for about 10 months. While in Jacksonville, the second biggest band in…
At the old Columbia Theater. I think it was on 47th Street, I don't remember where. Oh, right on Broadway. Yeah. Yeah, I remember.
